reuse.why: It extends the existing getExpectedScheduleAmount, but re-implements the 7.5% tolerance inline (Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075)) instead of calling the existing getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules.

duplication.why: The approximate-tolerance formula is duplicated from getApproxNumberThreshold, so the matching tolerance and the planning tolerance can drift apart.

placement.why: The rule extension sits in the shared amount helper in shared/schedules.ts where callers already resolve amounts.

scope.why: Only the helper, three of its callers and tests change.

maintainability.why: A hard-coded copy of the tolerance inside a nested ternary, plus an optional op that some callers (forecast, API, budget template) silently omit, makes the rule easy to apply inconsistently.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getExpectedScheduleAmount computes the tolerance inline instead of using getApproxNumberThreshold (shared/rules.ts).

disguised_duplication.where: getApproxNumberThreshold's Math.round(Math.abs(n) * 0.075) is inlined and reshaped as amount + Math.sign(amount) * Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075) in getExpectedScheduleAmount.

one_place.where: The rule is in getExpectedScheduleAmount behind an optional op, but forecast normalizeSchedule and the API's expectedAmount (api-models.ts) call it without op, and schedule-template.ts and the UI's getScheduledAmount compute amounts separately, so they keep the exact value.
